fatal_errors: The proposed TiVNbTa-to-TiVNbTaW modification does not reconstruct the target comparison between equiatomic CrFeTaVW and Ta-substituted CrFeTiVW.
It omits the target mechanical-alloying, spark-plasma-sintering, conventional-MD, and hybrid-MD/MC interventions.

The proposed solid-solution-strengthening mechanism is not the target mechanism involving MC energy minimization, W segregation, Fe2Ta Laves-phase formation, chemical disorder, and thermal diffusivity.
No cited prior HEA result supports the specific claim that approximately 5 at% W will preserve ductility while increasing TiVNbTa strength at 1273 K.
The prediction does not address the target thermal-diffusivity outcome or the experimentally observed phase constitutions.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses the broad divertor-interlayer motivation and supplies a controlled W-content series, an unmodified TiVNbTa control, and explicit mechanical failure criteria. However, it is scientifically disconnected from the hidden target in composition, intervention, mechanism, measurements, and outcomes. Its temperature range overlaps part of the target simulation range, but it does not reproduce the target processing conditions or 300–1000 K thermal-diffusivity testing. The experiment could test whether W improves strength, yet XRD and microscopy alone would not establish solid-solution inhibition of dislocation motion, so failure of the strength prediction would not uniquely falsify the proposed mechanism. The retained-ductility and phase-stability claims are speculative and unsupported by the listed prior HEA evidence.
